_about: The chat's commands, the same in both SDKs (2026-09-26, interactive-mode spec section 3.8).
commands: the table in menu order (name, usage, description, group, details). groups: the /help headings, in order.
keys: the key table. moved: a typed name that is not a command, and the command it became.
help: what /help prints at NO_COLOR and COLUMNS=100, line for line (the leading and trailing blank line left out).
help_command: what /help <command> prints, as the notice's lines. refusals: typed lines and the notice each gets, as lines.
tip: said after the card on the built-in agent in a folder with no agent file. outside: the last line of /help.

completion: the commands whose arguments the box completes after `/<command> ` (spec 3.8), and the first-level values each offers (both boxes must equal it; the second level comes from the folder, the keys, the schedules and the notes).

history: the typed-line history file both chats keep under the profile folder (S-291): its name, the folder and file modes, how many entries are kept, and one encoded sample in prompt_toolkit's FileHistory format that both chats must read back as `entries`.
Both chats' tables must equal this one; there is no source-parsing parity test any more.

completion._note: help searches the commands (several words: `/help sign in` finds login); agent also offers this folder's agents and the built-in one; skills add offers the names an agent file can name; keys set|remove the provider variables; cron run the agent's schedules; memory forget your notes; mcp list|add|remove, then add offers the servers other apps use and remove this agent's. resume offers this folder's conversations (none in a new folder, and then no delete either), rewind the folder's snapshots, model the models the agent may switch to (with no provider skill: the tiers and every known model). A row that completes the command runs it on enter (a conversation, a snapshot, a model, a command to explain, an agent, a key to set, a schedule, a note to forget: each of those asks before it changes anything); a verb, a skill, a key to remove and an MCP server are inserted, and a second enter sends the line. pickers: enter on the command itself opens its list when there is one to choose. (2026-09-26; search and pickers 2026-09-30.)

folders.about: Each folder its own lines (2026-09-29): ↑ and the suggestions offered every line typed under the profile, in any folder and by anything that ran the chat as its owner (an e2e test agent's prompts showed up in the owner's ↑). An entry now names the folder it was typed in on a comment line after its timestamp, which prompt_toolkit's FileHistory skips, and each chat offers only the lines of the folder it runs in (the real path). An entry written before folders were kept names none and is offered in no folder; it stays in the file, and a reader that ignores folders still reads every entry (`all`). Python: repl/session.py FolderHistory, parse_history_entries; TypeScript: cli/chat-history.ts parseChatHistoryEntries, readChatHistory(file, folder).

menu_search._about: How the menu finds rows by what is typed (2026-09-30, the owner: "/resume and other commands/subcommands should have search/filter on typing and up/down arrow selection"): the names the query starts, then the names it is inside, then the rows where every word of it starts a word of the name, the description or the hidden search text (words split at spaces and slashes, and into letters and digits), order kept within each group, case ignored. Command names are matched without their `/`, and command descriptions only from 2 characters. Read by python/tests/cli/test_chat_menu_search.py and typescript/tests/unit/cli/chat-menu-search.test.ts.
